audit_findings.title: Roku closing would invalidate the numerator, denominator and bridge simultaneously
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed consideration is $96.00 cash plus 0.9693 FOX Class A share per Roku share, supported by $12.0 billion of available bridge and term-loan commitments
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would add Roku earnings to OE, issue new FOX shares, consume cash, add acquisition debt and interest expense, and replace the current balance-sheet bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, FOX will pay $96.00 in cash and 0.9693 shares of FOX Class A Common Stock for each share of Roku Class A Common Stock and Roku Class B Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the merger.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated error in the explicitly AS_FILED valuation while the merger remains pending. It is a closing-dependent perimeter change that would make the current $1.717 billion OE anchor, 437.809 million-share denominator and $4.205 billion cash bridge mutually inconsistent. The net value direction cannot be determined without Roku's operating economics and the final financing and dilution.
audit_findings.action: Confirm transaction status; upon closing, rebuild OE from combined operations, calculate issued and fully diluted shares, and reconstruct cash, debt, interest expense and other bridge items from the closing balance sheet and financing terms.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats the entire cash balance as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $4.205 billion, or $9.60 per diluted share and 14.6% of the $28.792 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating, restricted or transaction-committed cash incorrectly classified as excess is added dollar-for-dollar to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The principal uses of cash that affect the Company’s liquidity position include the following: the acquisition of rights and related payments for entertainment and sports programming; operational expenditures including production costs; marketing and promotional expenses; expenses related to broadcasting the Company’s programming; employee and facility costs; capital expenditures; acquisitions, including redeemable noncontrolling interests; income taxes, interest and dividend payments; debt repayments; legal settlements; and stock repurchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated issue is that the bridge adds all filed cash without separating required liquidity from distributable excess. The record does not prove that all $4.205 billion must be excluded, so the actual correction remains unquantified. The maximum exposure is material: removing the full amount would reduce base value from $65.76 to about $56.16 per share, below the $58.42 market price.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash, restricted balances and committed uses—including programming, settlements, dividends and merger funding—and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Finite Disney tax benefits may have been capitalized into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed deferred-tax asset is $2.443 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE reflects reduced cash taxes from the Disney basis step-up, extrapolating the resulting OE through terminal value treats a finite tax shield as recurring operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: We also benefit from a tax asset that resulted from the step-up in the tax basis of our assets following the Disney Transaction, which is expected to provide an annual cash tax benefit for many years.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the tax asset is finite, but the supplied record does not establish how OE treated taxes, the annual cash benefit, or the utilization schedule. Accordingly, permanent overcapitalization is a plausible error rather than a demonstrated one. It could matter substantially because 49.7% of base operating value comes from terminal value, but the valuation overstatement cannot be quantified from the deferred-tax balance alone.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to cash taxes, obtain the remaining basis-step-up utilization schedule, forecast annual shield exhaustion and rerun explicit and terminal cash taxes at the normalized post-shield rate.

audit_findings.title: Smartmatic is a material unaccrued litigation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.7 billion claimed, equal to $6.17 per diluted share and 9.4% of base equity value; this is not an estimated loss
audit_findings.mechanism: A judgment or settlement would reduce the equity bridge directly, while recurring defense costs would reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: This includes the lawsuit filed by Smartmatic USA Corp. and certain of its affiliates (collectively, “Smartmatic”) in February 2021 seeking $ 2.7 billion in damages.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved contingency, not a demonstrated $2.7 billion liability: FOX reports the loss as neither probable nor reasonably estimable. Nevertheless, the filed claim is reasonably capable of changing the valuation assessment. A hypothetical full claimed-damages deduction would reduce base value from $65.76 to about $59.59 per share, leaving only about $1.17 above the quoted price, before defense costs or reputational effects.
audit_findings.action: Update the case's procedural status, rulings, trial timing, insurance and indemnification coverage, defense-cost run rate and counsel-supported exposure range; then scenario-weight the equity deduction and normalize recurring legal costs in OE.

audit_findings.title: The pending merger carries an omitted contingent termination claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.2 billion contingent fee, equal to $2.74 per diluted share and 4.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If a qualifying regulatory termination occurs, the fee becomes a cash claim against equity that is absent from both historical OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, FOX will be required to pay Roku a termination fee of approximately $1.2 billion if the Merger Agreement is terminated under certain circumstances related to the failure to obtain certain regulatory approvals or upon the entry of a permanent restraint under certain antitrust laws or investment screening laws.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual fee and its potential scale are demonstrated, but no supplied evidence establishes the probability of a qualifying regulatory failure. If paid in full, it would reduce base value from $65.76 to about $63.02 per share; whether its probability-weighted value is material cannot be established from the record. It should not be treated as a certain liability or as zero without a regulatory-status assessment.
audit_findings.action: Document regulatory milestones, antitrust and investment-screening developments, contractual trigger conditions and counsel-supported probability; rerun the bridge with explicit fee scenarios or a probability-weighted reserve.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable minority interests are outside permanent equity but absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $86 million, or $0.20 per diluted share and 0.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any redemption obligation not already captured through parent-attributable OE would be deducted from the common-equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are presented outside of permanent equity on the Company’s Balance Sheets as their redemption is outside the control of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The entire filed carrying amount is only 0.3% of the $28.792 billion base equity value and about $0.20 per share versus the $65.76 base estimate, so it cannot materially change the stated valuation conclusion on the current numbers. Contractual redemption value could differ from carrying value, but no larger amount is supplied.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the fiscal 2029 and 2030 put formulas and expected settlement values, and verify that minority earnings allocations and redemption cash flows are not double-counted; adjust the bridge if the calculated redemption value materially exceeds $86 million.
